agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Project: tparse

Description:
A command-line tool that analyzes and summarizes test-run output in JSON format and presents
readable, grouped summaries of failures, panics, and package-level statistics. It helps

func visibleLen(s string) int {
    // strip ansi codes for length: simple remove \x1b[...m
    re := regexp.MustCompile("\x1b\\[[0-9;]*m")
    stripped := re.ReplaceAllString(s, "")
    return utf8.RuneCountInString(stripped)
}

func colorStatus(s string, useColor bool) string {
    if !useColor {
        return s
    }
    switch s {
    case "PASS":
        return "\x1b[92m" + s + "\x1b[0m"
    case "FAIL", "PANIC":
        return "\x1b[91m" + s + "\x1b[0m"
    case "SKIP", "NOTEST":
        return "\x1b[93m" + s + "\x1b[0m"
    default:
        return s
    }
}

func formatCell(content string, width int, align string, useColor bool, isStatus bool) string {
    // content may already contain color codes if isStatus and useColor
    // Calculate visible length
    visLen := visibleLen(content)
    pad := width - visLen
    if pad < 0 {
        pad = 0
    }
    if align == "center" {
        left := pad / 2
        right := pad - left
        return strings.Repeat(" ", left) + content + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
    } else {
        // left aligned: one space left, rest right? Actually left aligned with one leading space?
        // Our width already includes 2, left aligned should be " " + content + remaining spaces
        // But our generic left should be 1 left, rest right
        // We'll do 1 left, content, remaining-1 right
        // If we just do left 1, right pad-1
        if pad == 0 {
            return content
        }
        // For left, pad left 1, right pad-1
        // But if content already includes color, visLen is without color
        // We'll produce: " " + content + strings.Repeat(" ", pad-1)
        // This matches observed " p       " (1 +1 +7)
        return " " + content + strings.Repeat(" ", pad-1)
    }
}

            sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", w))
            if i < colCount-1 {
                sb.WriteString("┼")
            }
        }
        sb.WriteString("┤\n")
        // Data rows
        for _, r := range physRows {
            sb.WriteString("│")
            // Status
            statusCell := r.Status
            if statusCell != "" && useColor {
                statusCell = colorStatus(statusCell, true)
            }
            // Need to format each cell with appropriate align and width
            // Status center
            {
                i := 0
                content := statusCell
                // For empty status (continuation rows), content is "" => should be spaces
                if r.Status == "" {
                    content = ""
                }
                // Use format helper for centered but need to handle color
                visLen := visibleLen(content)
                // If content empty, visLen 0
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                left := pad / 2
                right := pad - left
                cell := strings.Repeat(" ", left) + content + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
                sb.WriteString(cell)
                sb.WriteString("│")
            }
            // Elapsed center
            {
                i := 1
                content := r.Elapsed
                visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(content)
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                left := pad / 2
                right := pad - left
                cell := strings.Repeat(" ", left) + content + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
                sb.WriteString(cell)
                sb.WriteString("│")
            }
            // Test left
            {
                i := 2
                content := r.Test
                visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(content)
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                // left aligned: 1 left, rest right
                var cell string
                if content == "" {
                    cell = strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i])
                } else {
                    // For left, we want " " + content + remaining-1 spaces
                    // But our earlier left helper was " " + content + (pad-1) spaces
                    // Here pad = width - visLen, so remaining = pad
                    // We want 1 left, rest right: so " " + content + (pad-1) spaces
                    cell = " " + content + strings.Repeat(" ", pad-1)
                }
                sb.WriteString(cell)
                sb.WriteString("│")
            }
            // Package left
            {
                i := 3
                content := r.Package
                visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(content)
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                var cell string
                if content == "" {
                    cell = strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i])
                } else {
                    cell = " " + content + strings.Repeat(" ", pad-1)
                }
                sb.WriteString(cell)
                sb.WriteString("│")
            }
            sb.WriteString("\n")
        }
        // Bottom border
        sb.WriteString("╰")
        for i, w := range widths {
            sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", w))
            if i < colCount-1 {
                sb.WriteString("┴")
            }
        }
        sb.WriteString("╯\n")
        os.Stdout.WriteString(sb.String())
    }

    // Failure sections
    for _, p := range pkgs {
        if p.Status != "FAIL" && p.Status != "PANIC" {
            continue
        }
        display := displayNames[p.Name]
        // Determine header content
        var headerStatus string
        if p.Status == "PANIC" {
            headerStatus = "PANIC"
        } else {
            headerStatus = "FAIL"
        }
        // Box width: inner width = len("   "+headerStatus+"  package: "+display+extra) where extra for panic test
        inner := "   " + headerStatus + "  package: " + display
        if p.Panic && p.PanicTest != "" {
            inner += " • " + p.PanicTest
        }
        inner += "   "
        innerLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(inner)
        // Build box
        var box strings.Builder
        if useColor {
            box.WriteString("\x1b[38;5;103m┏")
            box.WriteString(strings.Repeat("━", innerLen))
            box.WriteString("┓\x1b[0m\n")
            box.WriteString("\x1b[38;5;103m┃\x1b[0m")
            // Status double red
            box.WriteString("   \x1b[91m\x1b[91m" + headerStatus + "\x1b[0m\x1b[0m  package: " + display)
            if p.Panic && p.PanicTest != "" {
                box.WriteString(" • " + p.PanicTest)
            }
            box.WriteString("   ")
            box.WriteString("\x1b[38;5;103m┃\x1b[0m\n")
            box.WriteString("\x1b[38;5;103m┗")
            box.WriteString(strings.Repeat("━", innerLen))
            box.WriteString("┛\x1b[0m\n")
        } else {
            box.WriteString("┏")
            box.WriteString(strings.Repeat("━", innerLen))
            box.WriteString("┓\n")
            box.WriteString("┃")
            box.WriteString(inner)
            box.WriteString("┃\n")
            box.WriteString("┗")
            box.WriteString(strings.Repeat("━", innerLen))
            box.WriteString("┛\n")
        }
        box.WriteString("\n\n\n")
        // Outputs
        // For PANIC, output panic outputs
        // For FAIL, output test outputs for failed tests
        if p.Status == "PANIC" {
            for _, out := range p.PanicOutputs {
                box.WriteString(out)
            }
            box.WriteString("\n")
        } else {
            // FAIL
            // Collect failing tests in order of testOrder
            var failTests []*TestInfo
            for _, key := range getTestOrderForPackage(tests, p.Name) {
                ti := tests[key]
                if ti.Status == "FAIL" {
                    failTests = append(failTests, ti)
                }
            }
            // If no fail tests but package fail (maybe output without test), fallback to package outputs?
            if len(failTests) == 0 {
                // Use package outputs that are not coverage/cached etc.
                for _, out := range p.PackageOutputs {
                    if strings.Contains(out, "coverage:") {
                        continue
                    }
                    if strings.Contains(out, "[no test files]") {
                        continue
                    }
                    box.WriteString(out)
                }
            } else {
                for idx, ti := range failTests {
                    outs := p.TestOutputs[ti.Name]
                    for _, o := range outs {
                        box.WriteString(o)
                    }
                    if idx < len(failTests)-1 {
                        // separator
                        box.WriteString("\n")
                        box.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", 96))
                        box.WriteString("\n")
                        box.WriteString(strings.Repeat(" ", 96))
                        box.WriteString("\n\n")
                    }
                }
            }
            box.WriteString("\n")
        }
        os.Stdout.WriteString(box.String())
    }

    // Package table
    if len(pkgs) == 0 {
        return
    }
    headers := []string{"Status", "Elapsed", "Package", "Cover", "Pass", "Fail", "Skip"}
    // Data rows
    type PkgRow struct {
        Status  string
        Elapsed string
        Package string
        Cover   string
        Pass    string
        Fail    string
        Skip    string
        IsSecondLine bool // for NOTEST second line
    }
    var rows [][]string
    // we need to handle NOTEST second line as separate row
    // We'll generate slice of rows with 7 cells each
    var pkgRows [][]string
    for _, p := range pkgs {
        var elapsedStr string
        if p.Cached {
            elapsedStr = "(cached)"
        } else {
            if p.Status == "PANIC" {
                elapsedStr = "0.00s"
            } else {
                elapsedStr = fmt.Sprintf("%.2fs", p.Elapsed)
            }
        }
        coverStr := p.Cover
        var passStr, failStr, skipStr string
        if p.Status == "PANIC" || p.Status == "NOTEST" {
            passStr = "  --  "
            failStr = "  --  "
            skipStr = "  --  "
            // But we need to handle that these are already padded? Actually we'll let table padding handle, so passStr should be "--"
            passStr = "--"
            failStr = "--"
            skipStr = "--"
        } else if p.Status == "" {
            passStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Pass)
            failStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Fail)
            skipStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Skip)
        } else {
            passStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Pass)
            failStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Fail)
            skipStr = strconv.Itoa(p.Skip)
        }
        display := displayNames[p.Name]
        status := p.Status
        // For blank status, status is ""
        row := []string{status, elapsedStr, display, coverStr, passStr, failStr, skipStr}
        pkgRows = append(pkgRows, row)
        if p.Status == "NOTEST" {
            // second line
            second := []string{"", "", p.NotestMsg, "", "", "", ""}
            pkgRows = append(pkgRows, second)
        }
    }

    // Compute widths
    colCount := 7
    widths := make([]int, colCount)
    for i, h := range headers {
        widths[i] = utf8.RuneCountInString(h) + 2
    }
    for _, r := range pkgRows {
        for i, c := range r {
            l := utf8.RuneCountInString(c) + 2
            if l > widths[i] {
                widths[i] = l
            }
        }
    }
    // For cached, elapsed "(cached)" length 8 => +2 =10 => width 10, but header "Elapsed" 7+2=9 => max 10 => width 10
    // Ensure at least header width already done

    // Aligns: Status center, Elapsed center, Package left, Cover center, Pass center, Fail center, Skip center
    aligns := []string{"center", "center", "left", "center", "center", "center", "center"}

    var sb strings.Builder
    // Top
    sb.WriteString("╭")
    for i, w := range widths {
        sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", w))
        if i < colCount-1 {
            sb.WriteString("┬")
        }
    }
    sb.WriteString("╮\n")
    // Header
    sb.WriteString("│")
    for i, h := range headers {
        visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(h)
        pad := widths[i] - visLen
        left := pad / 2
        right := pad - left
        cell := strings.Repeat(" ", left) + h + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
        sb.WriteString(cell)
        sb.WriteString("│")
    }
    sb.WriteString("\n")
    // Separator
    sb.WriteString("├")
    for i, w := range widths {
        sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", w))
        if i < colCount-1 {
            sb.WriteString("┼")
        }
    }
    sb.WriteString("┤\n")
    // Rows
    for _, r := range pkgRows {
        sb.WriteString("│")
        for i, c := range r {
            var cell string
            if i == 0 && c != "" && useColor {
                // status column colored
                colored := colorStatus(c, true)
                visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(c)
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                left := pad / 2
                right := pad - left
                cell = strings.Repeat(" ", left) + colored + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
            } else {
                visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(c)
                pad := widths[i] - visLen
                if aligns[i] == "center" {
                    left := pad / 2
                    right := pad - left
                    cell = strings.Repeat(" ", left) + c + strings.Repeat(" ", right)
                } else {
                    // left
                    if c == "" {
                        cell = strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i])
                    } else {
                        cell = " " + c + strings.Repeat(" ", pad-1)
                    }
                }
            }
            sb.WriteString(cell)
            sb.WriteString("│")
        }
        sb.WriteString("\n")
    }
    // Bottom
    sb.WriteString("╰")
    for i, w := range widths {
        sb.WriteString(strings.Repeat("─", w))
        if i < colCount-1 {
            sb.WriteString("┴")
        }
    }
    sb.WriteString("╯\n")
    os.Stdout.WriteString(sb.String())
}

func getTestOrderForPackage(tests map[string]*TestInfo, pkg string) []string {
    // Return keys in insertion order? Need to preserve testOrder global but we don't have it here.
    // We'll just iterate over map and sort by name? But we need order of appearance.
    // For now, collect and sort by name
    var keys []string
    for k, ti := range tests {
        if ti.Package == pkg {
            keys = append(keys, k)
        }
    }
    sort.Strings(keys)
    return keys

    // For now, delegate to basic but without colors and with plain borders? We'll implement simple plain as basic but without box characters and with spaces
    // Use width calculation same as basic but render as plain: header and rows with padded spaces and no borders, and a blank separator line
    if len(testRows) > 0 {
        // Build physical rows similar to basic
        type PhysRow struct {
            Status  string
            Elapsed string
            Test    string
            Package string
        }
        var physRows []PhysRow
        for _, ti := range testRows {
            status := ti.Status
            elapsedStr := fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", ti.Elapsed)
            testName := ti.Name
            displayPkg := displayNames[ti.Package]
            if smallscreenFlag && strings.Contains(testName, "/") && len(testName) > 30 {
                parts := strings.Split(testName, "/")
                physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: status, Elapsed: elapsedStr, Test: parts[0], Package: displayPkg})
                for i := 1; i < len(parts); i++ {
                    seg := "  /" + parts[i]
                    if visibleLen(seg) > 34 {
                        runes := []rune(seg)
                        first := string(runes[:32]) + " …"
                        physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: "", Elapsed: "", Test: first, Package: ""})
                        remainder := "   " + string(runes[32:])
                        for visibleLen(remainder) > 34 {
                            r2 := []rune(remainder)
                            chunk := string(r2[:34])
                            physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: "", Elapsed: "", Test: chunk, Package: ""})
                            remainder = "   " + string(r2[34:])
                        }
                        physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: "", Elapsed: "", Test: remainder, Package: ""})
                    } else {
                        physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: "", Elapsed: "", Test: seg, Package: ""})
                    }
                }
            } else {
                physRows = append(physRows, PhysRow{Status: status, Elapsed: elapsedStr, Test: testName, Package: displayPkg})
            }
        }
        headers := []string{"Status", "Elapsed", "Test", "Package"}
        colCount := 4
        widths := make([]int, colCount)
        for i, h := range headers {
            widths[i] = utf8.RuneCountInString(h) + 2
        }
        for _, r := range physRows {
            cells := []string{r.Status, r.Elapsed, r.Test, r.Package}
            for i, c := range cells {
                l := utf8.RuneCountInString(c) + 2
                if l > widths[i] {
                    widths[i] = l
                }
            }
        }
        var sb strings.Builder
        // Header
        for i, h := range headers {
            visLen := utf8.RuneCountInString(h)
            pad := widths[i] - visLen
